correctness.rationale: Using \(L=D-W\), the first-order double commutator gives \(\rho_{jj}=1-\gamma s_2t+O(t^2)\) and \(Q\rho Q=\gamma t\,(QL|j\rangle)(\langle j|LQ)+O(t^2)\). Multiplying by classical square roots creates the single nontrivial order-t² eigenvalue \(\gamma s_3t^2\); the root fidelity then yields \(c=s_1+\gamma s_2-2\sqrt{\gamma s_3}\). Exact \(K_{a,b}\) projections have masses \(1/N\), \(b/(aN)\), \((a-1)/a\) even if \(a=b\). The derivative of their terminal square-root sum is negative for \(a\ge2\), while \(c_\gamma(d)\) strictly increases, so the two localized distances reverse order for \(2\le m<n\). Continuity proves existence of at least one finite crossing for every real \(\gamma>0\). Independent finite spectral tests run with final included code: 576 pinching sites, 9998 topology, 225 weighted slopes and 12 reversal examples. Tests are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The initial-position optimization for noisy coherent walks is operationally motivated by the fidelity QC benchmark. Universal switching on every nonstar unbalanced biclique for all positive intrinsic-noise strengths is a topology-controlled physical boundary not a numerical example or arbitrary parameter slice; sharp fixed-size star and balanced graph extrema are included. Exact first-order weighted formula makes the mechanism transparent and suggests where similar crossings may arise, without speculative claims of experimental utility.
